sources.label: Swing-trade signals
sources.caveat: Rule output on daily bars, not a recommendation. It carries no position sizing or risk limits, and most rows are positions already open rather than fresh buys. Measured on 12 broad and sector ETFs (survivorship-free) 2019-01-01..2025-07-01, this strategy returned 49.4% against 145.6% for simply holding the same universe, at Sharpe 0.47 against 0.80. It beat same-window buy-and-hold in 3 of 17 walk-forward windows. What does hold up is drawdown: -31.6% against -35.8% for the benchmark.

sources.label: Polymarket BTC 5-min binaries
sources.caveat: Publishes an observation, not picks. The repo's own backtest on real fills found the market's own price forecasts the settlement BETTER than the model, and that what survives costs is feed latency rather than the pricing model. Simulation only -- the repo has no order-placement path. Latest scan: model Brier 0.1594 vs market 0.1539, so the market is ahead (lower is better). Post-cost returns cross zero at 3.3s of BTC feed staleness, against a 3.75s decision cadence.

methodology: A digest: the top 3 from each scanner, so one glance shows what is live right now. Each scanner runs on its own schedule and publishes its own full panel; this merges them and runs nothing itself, so a slow source can only make its own row go quiet. Items are ranked WITHIN a source and there is deliberately no cross-source score -- basis points, an earnings yield and a contract cadence are not commensurable, and one leaderboard over them would be invented. Every section carries its own caveat; read it before the numbers. Nothing here is advice, none of it is an executed trade, and a section that has gone stale shows nothing rather than yesterday's numbers.
